data.title: The fortress of Nové Zámky – a 3D reconstruction
data.excerpt: The first fortress at Nové Zámky was built in 1545 on the left bank of the River Nitra and belonged to the Hungarian system of castles and fortresses raised against the Turks. In 1663 the new fortress fell to the Ottoman army despite a stubborn defence, and our member Igor Furugláš has brought it back to life in a 3D visualisation.
data.metaTitle: The fortress of Nové Zámky – a 3D reconstruction
data.metaDescription: A 3D reconstruction of the anti-Ottoman fortress of Nové Zámky, built in 1545 on the River Nitra and taken by the Turkish army in 1663.

blocks.text:
God admonished us a thousand years past,
when there was written the six hundred sixty-third.
There came the Turk, the Tatar, a cruel enemy,
and quartered his army below Nové Zámky.

Since we would not fear the Lord God,
nor love our neighbour as ourselves with our hearts,
nor walk here according to His commandments,
but trod His holy word underfoot,

dwelling safely in our dear homeland,
giving no thought to any misfortune of ours,
taking our pleasure in the delights of the flesh,
following nothing but greed and pride.

children.text: The first fortress at Nové Zámky was built by decision of the Archbishop of Esztergom Pál Várday to defend his estates, on the left bank of the River Nitra, in 1545. It belonged to the Hungarian defensive system of castles and fortresses raised to protect against the Turks. After its destruction a new fortress was built, which, however, despite a stubborn defence could not withstand the superior numbers of the Turkish army in 1663.

A member and collaborator of our association, Igor Furugláš, decided to bring this important ancient fortress back to life by means of a 3D visualisation; its fall meant many years of subjection to the Turks for the Kingdom of Hungary. We have tried to keep to the surviving parameters of the fortifications and of the buildings inside them as they are known today. The commentary for the video was recorded for us by the actor and director of the
Ján Harry Haruštiak, for which he has our great thanks. Judge for yourselves whether the reconstruction has come off...
